problems: test_memory_decreases_after_unload is non-deterministic and order-dependent. LocalTransformersProvider(prefer_xpu=True) uses the global ModelCache by default. When run after the session-scoped loaded_xpu_provider fixture has already loaded TinyLlama, the fresh provider's _ensure_model_loaded hits the global cache and obtains the same LoadedModel object that the session provider also holds alive. After unload_model(), that session reference keeps model tensors live on XPU; torch.xpu.empty_cache() cannot reclaim referenced memory. get_xpu_memory_info(0) therefore reports the same allocated bytes before and after the unload, causing 'assert allocated_after < allocated_before' to fail spuriously even when the production code is correct. The mutation (removing _release_device_caches) would also not reliably flip this test in a session context, since the assertion was already failing. Fix: pass a freshly constructed ModelCache() to the LocalTransformersProvider constructor so the test provider's model load is completely isolated from the session-scoped cache — the model is loaded as a new allocation on XPU, and when unloaded (with only that one reference) the memory is actually freed.

per_finding_notagate.reason: The test is non-deterministic and order-dependent due to shared global ModelCache state. The fresh provider is created with 'LocalTransformersProvider(prefer_xpu=True)' which at __init__ line 194 calls 'self._model_cache = model_cache or get_global_model_cache()' — the global cache, not a dedicated one. When run in the same session as the session-scoped loaded_xpu_provider fixture (which loads TinyLlama into the global cache), the fresh provider's _ensure_model_loaded call hits the global cache at load_model_for_xpu:490-492 and returns the SAME LoadedModel object that loaded_xpu_provider._loaded_model also references. After unload_model() drops the fresh provider's reference and removes the entry from the ModelCache dict, the session provider still holds a live Python reference to the model tensors on XPU. torch.xpu.empty_cache() cannot free memory still referenced by live tensors. Therefore get_xpu_memory_info(0) returns the same allocated bytes before and after unload, and 'assert allocated_after < allocated_before' fails spuriously — the production code is correct but the test reports failure due to shared state. In an isolated run (no session provider present), the test would work correctly. The mutation (remove _release_device_caches) would then also NOT consistently flip the test when run in session context because the assertion was already failing. The fix requires passing a dedicated 'ModelCache()' instance to the fresh provider constructor so the model load allocates new device memory independently of the session-scoped model, giving true before/after isolation.
